newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: SOCCER-AUSTRIA AND CROATIA CONSIDER JOINT BID FOR EURO 2004.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AUSTRIA AND CROATIA CONSIDER JOINT BID FOR EURO 2004.

text.p: Austrian and Croatian soccer officials met in Vienna on Monday to discuss a possible joint bid from the two countries to host the European soccer championships in 2004.
Austrian federation chairman Beppo Mauhart said the two countries would remain in contact about the matter and that a final decision would be taken in April 1997.
Earlier in the month, Mauhart negotiated with Czech, Hungarian and Swiss soccer federations on the possibility of co-hosting the tournament.

"It is impossible for us to to organise a tournament with 16 teams on our own, therefore we are looking for a partner," said Mauhart. "The trend at the moment is to let small countries organise the tournament together."
On Monday, Mauhart met with Croatian soccer federation president Josip Soic, vice-president Vlatko Markovic and general secretary Josip Cop.
One obvious problem facing the bid is that the two countries do not share a common border. Although they are situated close together, they are separated by Slovenia.

Croatia already has two stadiums seating 50,000 in Agram and Split, as well as arenas for 30,000 in Osijek, Rijeka, Varazdin and Agram. Austria's biggest stadium is the 62,000 capacity Ernst Happel Stadium in Vienna, where the 1995 European Cup final, among other big games, has been staged.
According to Mauhart, Croatian soccer officials will be seeking financial support from their government within the next few days to build more stadiums.

The government of the Czech Republic has already pledged its financial support for the project -- which could mean that some matches are staged in a third country. The Czechs reached the final of Euro 96 where they lost to Germany. The former Czechoslovakia won the tournament in 1976.
UEFA, European soccer's governing body, is expected to make a decision on the bids for the 2004 championships -- in which Spain is considered a possible front runner -- in 1998.
Belgium and the Netherlands will jointly host the competition in 2000.
